title: Why, how and what
heading: Why · How · What
caption: AI speeds the work up, so the pressure moves into specifying and review: why that matters, how to play it, and what every work center shows.

why.title: AI at one work center floods the next inspection.
why.caption: <amplifies>AI amplifies what the organization already is</amplifies>. With AI at the engineer alone, quality assurance piles up and the Customer gets far less. <pain>Incomplete requirements were always the most named pain</pain>, and they come back as rework; clear requirements, good orders, lower the pressure.

how.title: Ideal, Realistic, then a scenario's tour.
how.caption: Ideal, then Realistic; each scenario's tour sets the dials and runs to the week that matters; a click on a work center opens its dashboard.

what.title: Every work center has two dials.
what.caption: Efficiency is output, how much it puts out; effectiveness is outcome, how much of it is good. AI raises the first and leaves the second alone. <hard>Specifying was always the hard part</hard>, and <people>every work center is people and tools</people>.

why-you-may-leave-it.title: Why you may leave it
why-you-may-leave-it.script: If you played it, you already have the picture, so this is the short version. One slide covers why it matters, how to use it and what it shows.

why-the-problem-is-the-system.title: Why: the problem is the system
why-the-problem-is-the-system.keywords: unclear requirements, nobody to blame, review, neighbours, specifying, hypothesis
why-the-problem-is-the-system.script: Unclear requirements were always expensive, and nobody in the chain was to blame for that. AI speeds execution up, so the work piles up at review, and my picture is that it spreads to the neighbours. This next part is my hypothesis: the effort moves into specifying too, because that was always the hard part, and nobody has measured it yet.

clear-orders-lower-it.title: Clear orders lower it
clear-orders-lower-it.keywords: clear requirements, good orders, feed it something worth moving
clear-orders-lower-it.script: Clear requirements are good orders for the factory. AI moves whatever you feed it, faster, so feed it something worth moving.

how-play-it.title: How: play it
how-play-it.keywords: Ideal, Realistic, scenario, guided tour, dials, dashboard
how-play-it.script: It starts in Ideal, then Realistic, and every scenario has a guided tour that sets the dials and runs to the week that matters; a click on any work center opens its dashboard.

what-two-dials-everywhere.title: What: two dials everywhere
what-two-dials-everywhere.keywords: efficiency, effectiveness, AI raises the first, review, pressure
what-two-dials-everywhere.script: Every work center has efficiency, how much it puts out, and effectiveness, how much of it is good. AI raises the first and leaves the second alone. Review stays as fast as it was, so that is where the pressure builds.

take-it-back-to-monday.title: Take it back to Monday
take-it-back-to-monday.keywords: map your team, check the review step, write the requirement, process owner
take-it-back-to-monday.script: Map your team, check the review step before you speed anything up, and write the requirement for someone new. Whoever owns that process knows where the pressure lands first.

ai-amplifies.description: AI's primary role is as an amplifier of an organization's existing strengths and weaknesses, and the greatest returns come from the underlying organizational system rather than the tools [1] (AIE-0018).

dora-2025.title: DORA, State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025 (overview page)

incomplete-requirements.header: Incomplete requirements are the most named pain
incomplete-requirements.description: 48% of 228 companies named incomplete or hidden requirements their most frequent requirements problem, with rework after implementation among the reported effects. Self-reported survey; frequency is not cost [1] (SWE-0002).

mendez-naming-the-pain.title: Méndez Fernández et al., Naming the Pain in Requirements Engineering: Contemporary Problems, Causes, and Effects in Practice

specifying-is-hard.description: Deciding precisely what to build is the hardest single part of building software. That AI moves the saved effort into specifying is an inference from this and the review findings; no source measures specification effort rising [1] (AIE-0018, AIE-0020).

brooks-no-silver-bullet.title: Brooks, No Silver Bullet: Essence and Accident in Software Engineering

people-and-technology.header: A work center is people and technology
people-and-technology.description: A socio-technical system is a system made of people and technology, and an organization's structure shapes what it builds. The definitions are the speaker's paraphrase [1] (SWE-0001).

bender-tipping-point.title: Adam Bender, Software Engineering at the Tipping Point (conference talk, transcript)
